facts.timeline_arc: From June 2025 Nvidia surged to a record market value as it expanded AI chips into drug discovery and supercomputing, then in July it intensified its China push with a made‑for‑China chip and high‑level visits. August brought export‑licence constraints that forced revenue‑sharing deals, while September saw sweeping hardware alliances with Intel and OpenAI and a public stance on immigration policy. The first half of 2026 was marked by record revenue, a massive $80 billion buyback, and a suite of collaborations that cemented its AI infrastructure leadership, followed by a $2 billion pledge to broaden custom AI chip access and growing competition from new wafer‑scale entrants. Throughout, Nvidia’s strategy oscillated between expanding market reach, navigating geopolitical regulation, and reinforcing its hardware dominance.

turning_points.why: Nvidia hit a record market value and announced major AI‑driven partnerships in drug discovery and supercomputing.
The company launched a made‑for‑China chip and CEO Jensen Huang made a third Beijing visit, signaling a strategic China push amid US‑China rivalry.
Nvidia sealed a joint effort with Intel on custom data‑center products and a partnership with OpenAI to power at least 10 GW of AI data centers.
It reported an 85% jump in quarterly revenue, announced an $80 billion share buyback and raised its dividend, calming investor concerns.
Nvidia launched the Groq 3 LPU and announced extensive collaborations with telecom, tech firms and IBM to build next‑generation AI‑native networks.
The company supplied chips for Nokia's 5G rollout while facing heightened competition from new wafer‑scale AI chip makers such as the model.

text.summary: NVIDIA drew 215,943 articles across the window from 2024-06 to 2026-05, of which 152,441 were high-priority stories. It ranks first among the four companies compared for attention, with 46.3% of peer coverage. Coverage is dominated by technology and finance themes, with AI the largest business lens at 36.0% of articles. The recent record is one of record revenue, an $80 billion buyback, and new partnerships, set against export-licence constraints and China-related coverage. Competition from new wafer-scale AI chip makers such as the model appears in the latest turning points. The story has moved from a gaming and hardware identity towards finance, economy and geopolitics.
